descriptionChirho: Intransitive turning of a subject: turning around, turning back, turning aside, or changing one's facing direction, including withdrawal and evasive turning (Qal stem; Arabic dara, iltafata, inhaarafa).
To encircle or surround a person, place, or object, including hostile besieging and protective encompassing (Qal stem with object; Arabic ahata).
To travel around, make a circuit, go about, patrol, or march around an area, emphasizing traversal of a path rather than static encirclement (Qal stem; Arabic tafa, dara).
Reflexive or middle-voice turning: a border winds around, something turns of its own accord, a boundary line shifts direction (Niphal stem; Arabic dara, imtadda).
Intensified encompassing or repeated circling: to surround closely, to go around ceremonially or repeatedly (Piel stem; Arabic ahata, tafa).
Causative turning or transforming: to turn something or someone, to change, divert, or redirect, including turning faces and hearts (Hifil stem; Arabic hawwala, ghayyara).
Causative movement of an object or person from one place to another: to bring around, lead around, remove, or relocate (Hifil stem; Arabic naqala, adara).
Passive of the causative: to be turned by an external agent, to be changed or transformed passively (Hofal stem; Arabic ghuyyira).
Rare intransitive change of state: physical turning extended metaphorically to transformation or alteration of condition (Qal stem; Arabic tahawwala).
